How much do ATMs charge on Koh Samui? | Most Thai banks charge foreign cards 220–250 THB per withdrawal, and AEON ATMs inside Big C, Lotus's and Makro charge 150 THB. Your own bank may add a fee and exchange margin on top, so take out larger amounts less often.
Which ATM is cheapest in Thailand? | AEON ATMs, at 150 THB per withdrawal for foreign cards, with a 20,000 THB limit. If you want the most cash per fee, Krungsri ATMs allow up to 30,000 THB per withdrawal, but charge 220–250 THB.
Should I accept conversion at the ATM? | No. Always decline conversion and choose to be charged in THB. The ATM's conversion rate (dynamic currency conversion) is usually several percent worse than your own bank's rate.
Can I pay by card on Koh Samui? | Yes, in malls, supermarkets, 7-Eleven, hotels and most restaurants in Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai. Street food, markets, songthaews, most taxis, scooter rentals and national park fees need cash.
Where can I exchange money on Koh Samui? | At bank exchange booths along Chaweng Beach Road, in Lamai and at Central Samui, or at licensed money changers. Bring your passport and clean, undamaged notes, and compare rates on the boards.
Can a foreigner open a bank account in Thailand? | Usually only with a long-stay visa or extension, such as Non-O, Non-B with a work permit or a DTV, plus proof of address and a Thai phone number. Requirements vary by bank and branch; tourists on a visa exemption are usually refused.
How much cash do I need for boat trips? | The Ang Thong park fee is 300 THB per adult and 150 THB per child, Koh Madsum (Pig Island) is about 50 THB, and Koh Nang Yuan is 250 THB per adult (120 THB per child), all cash on the day. Add a little for drinks, snacks and extras.
Is there a limit on bringing cash into Thailand? | There is no limit, but you must declare foreign currency worth more than USD 20,000, or more than 450,000 THB in Thai baht, to customs. Taking Thai baht out is limited to 50,000 THB per person without Bank of Thailand permission.
